title: year 3 · the ranges
hook: this part of the path is still being planned: a map with a dotted line, and a verse about steps that are never lost
tomorrow: the Devi Mahatmya (13 chapters, read whole)

segments.voice: Yesterday: the year close, and the lake where Yudhishthira wondered that the living forget they are the ones who remain.

On a trail map, there's a moment where the solid red line turns into a dotted one. The trail goes on. Someone has walked it and marked it. But the map is saying, honestly, the details here are still being worked out. That's where the path stands tonight. The next ranges are drawn: the goddess, Shiva, the schools of thought, the Vedas, the women of the epics, the regional traditions. The lessons themselves are still being written and checked. So the last day of year three is a good day for one honest verse about walking into a dotted line.
screen: `THE SOLID LINE TURNS DOTTED.` → `THE RANGES ARE DRAWN.` → `THE LESSONS STILL BEING WRITTEN.`

segments.voice: The verse is from the Bhagavad Gita, in the second chapter, which this year re-read in its place on the battlefield. Krishna has just told Arjuna he's about to hear a new way of understanding action, and before he explains it, he gives a promise. In paraphrase: on this path, no effort begun is lost, and no harm comes of it. Even a little of this dharma protects you from great fear. The Gita doesn't say finish the path and then you'll be safe. It says even a little of it protects. Some teachers read that generously: the half-managed sit, the missed week, the story whose ending slipped away, none of it is wasted. In the verse's own picture, whatever was walked stays walked. Commentators read the verse in more than one way. Some hear it about the steadied mind Krishna is about to describe: action done without grasping at results. Others hear it about any honest start on a spiritual path. Either way, it's a verse made for beginnings. And year three has been full of people who walked into country no one had mapped for them: Yudhishthira at a lake with a voice in the water, Mirabai walking out of palace rules, Ramana, a boy who left home for a holy hill. Tomorrow year four begins with the Devi, the goddess, and a text read from start to finish. A new range, and an old promise to carry into it.
screen: `A DOTTED LINE ON THE MAP.` · `NO EFFORT ON THIS PATH IS LOST.` · `EVEN A LITTLE PROTECTS FROM GREAT FEAR.` · `YEAR FOUR BEGINS WITH THE DEVI.` · then, large: `WHAT WAS WALKED STAYS WALKED.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind one small thing you did on this path this year, even something you think didn't count, one sit, one story, one minute of attention, and let it be enough. Then turn gently to face what's ahead without planning it: just the next step, and the breath that carries you there. If you pray, bring the coming year before God, or the goddess, in your own words; if you don't, let tomorrow have a little room.
Year three. The great story and the saints, now walked, and kept. And the ranges beyond it, drawn on the map, still being written.
Your line: year three, the ranges. Even a little counts. Day one thousand sixty-one: year three, done.

screen: `DAY 1061 COUNTS.` → `YEAR 3, DONE.` → `TOMORROW: THE DEVI MAHATMYA (13 CHAPTERS, READ WHOLE).`

notes: Last day of year three; the index hook is 'this part of the path is still being planned'. The script says honestly that year four's ranges are drawn in the outline but its lessons are still being written and checked. No Keeper approval is implied.

Editor pass: review now matches 1060's corrected reading of the Yaksha answer; 2.40 is mid-chapter, so 'early in the second chapter' became 'in the second chapter'; 'no harm comes from turning back' (a stretch for pratyavāyo na vidyate) became 'no harm comes of it' in the teach and fork reveal; the loose 'Andal singing to a god she'd never seen' was replaced with Mirabai walking out of palace rules (as taught on 1049); howItsDone 'often' softened.

Audit (2026-10-01): the narrator applied 2.40 directly to the listener as a promise ('No effort is lost. Not the sit you only half managed... Whatever was walked stays walked'), which states a religious promise as fact; now attributed ('some teachers read that generously... in the verse's own picture'). 'Ramana, a boy alone with one question' conflated his teenage experience with the later who-am-I teaching (1050); now 'a boy who left home for a holy hill' (Arunachala). Confirm.

Gita 2.40 paraphrased (nehābhikramanāśo 'sti pratyavāyo na vidyate / svalpam apy asya dharmasya trāyate mahato bhayāt). 'No harm comes from turning back' renders pratyavāyo na vidyate; some translate it 'no adverse result' or 'no obstacle'. Arnold 1885 not quoted because exact wording was not certain. Confirm.
Context: 2.39 introduces buddhi-yoga, the teaching about to be given; 'a new way of understanding action' is a simplification. Two commentarial readings given without ranking; confirm they are fair.
'Which this year re-read in its place on the battlefield' refers to the Bhishma Parva Gita sessions in the year-three outline; confirm they covered chapter 2.
Ramana as 'a boy alone with one question' refers to his teenage death experience; confirm it matches how the path told it. Andal 'singing to a god she'd never seen' is a loose description; confirm.
The tomorrow title includes '13 chapters' from the index; the count is not spoken in the voice.
